classInfo.title: Tuck Handstand Focus
classInfo.description: If you’re looking to learn to get into a handstand, this 15-minute, no-equipment-needed class will introduce you to jumping into a tuck handstand. You can practice this anywhere to build your balance!

classInfo.title: Single Bar Shoulder Mobility
classInfo.description: All you need is a single bar and a pair of rings to create mobility in the shoulders through hanging, twisting, and pulling. This 10-minute follow-along is the perfect addition to any upper body strength training–use it for warm up, cool down, or on a recovery day to keep your shoulders happy!

classInfo.title: Rows Triplex
classInfo.description: Build your pulling power and sculpt your core with this fun and challenging workout! You’ll build strength for a stellar rope climb while also developing control over your midsection.

classInfo.title: Knee Series
classInfo.description: Knee pain is NOT inevitable! In 15 minutes you can strengthen the muscles, tendons, and ligaments of the knees, significantly decrease your injury risk, and improve your knee health. Prepare your knees for the unexpected twists and turns of life using this series—you’ll be happy that you did!

classInfo.title: Hanging Leg Lifts Triplex
classInfo.description: Have less than five minutes to spare? You can still fit in this fiery core routine! Have a bit more time? Consider completing a few rounds for a real burner!

classInfo.title: Extended Warmup
classInfo.description: This 25-minute warm-up will create heat in your body from head to toe, while focusing on active and engaging stretches to increase your flexibility while getting you fired up!

classInfo.title: Daily Limber
classInfo.description: This 5-minute routine will loosen your muscles, increase blood flow to your joints, prepare your body for exercise, and aid in recovery. Say goodbye to stiff, locked up limbs and crackly joints–embrace this seriously healthy habit for impressive mobility!

classInfo.title: Core Sequence
classInfo.description: A short but powerful 4-minute routine that can be done at home daily to light up your entire core! Expect to work hard in this no-excuse sequence for solid abs.

classInfo.title: Beginner Mobility Drills
classInfo.description: Swing, swivel, and lean your way to healthy movement with this gentle mobility routine! Create warmth through the back, chest, shoulders, and hips to boost blood flow and energize the body during this sequence.

classInfo.title: 30 Minute Legs
classInfo.description: Follow along for 30 minutes to lengthen and strengthen your legs from hip to toe! Strength building exercises create muscle and tone throughout the legs, while active limbering movements stretch and relieve tight muscles.

classInfo.title: 25 Minute Core Workout
classInfo.description: Test your core endurance with this 25-minute workout focused on longer holds and full abdominal engagement. Hollow Body and Arch Body Holds may be the main event, but you’ll feel the heat from head to toe!

classInfo.title: 20 Minute Handstands
classInfo.description: Get upside down with this 20-minute handstand workout! First, we’ll focus on prepping key areas, including the shoulders and wrists, before we practice body positions inverted on the wall.

classInfo.title: Foundation Core
classInfo.description: A powerful core curriculum so effective that washboard abs are just a side note. Strength and stability here transfers to better movement throughout the body. Your entire core will be conditioned so far beyond traditional crunches you’ll never consider going back!

classInfo.title: Middle Split
classInfo.description: Everyone can start building the mobility necessary for the middle splits and pancake–no matter what your flexibility level is! This 45-minute sequence will help you find relief and develop flexibility throughout your lower body.

classInfo.title: Foundation Lower Body
classInfo.description: 17 potent leg strengthening exercises intertwined with hip, knee, and ankle mobility, take you from introductory squatting, all the way to single-leg pistol squats and advanced weighted leg strength. We don’t recommend performing any weighted leg work until you’ve reached the advanced level of this progression plan.

classInfo.title: Front Split
classInfo.description: A perfect 45-minute mobility routine for athletes and office workers alike! Tension in the quads, hip flexors, feet, calves, and hamstrings will rapidly disappear with continued use of this sequence. If Front Splits are your goal, start here!

classInfo.title: Foundation Upper Body
classInfo.description: The best of both worlds: push, pull, and planche your way to unrivaled levels of strength while mobilizing and preventing injury. 150 progressions will take you as far you want to go, whether that’s tight and toned or massive and muscular.

classInfo.title: Thoracic Bridge
classInfo.description: Fight the negative effects of sitting by opening up your shoulders and thoracic spine during this 45-minute guided stretch session. Steadily build towards a full thoracic bridge while creating health throughout your shoulders and upper back.

classInfo.title: Handstand
classInfo.description: More than 25 handstand exercises, each with accompanying mobility drills, to take you from basic inversions to a perfect handstand line. Indestructible wrists, and bulletproof shoulders included.

classInfo.title: Movement
classInfo.description: The most important and functional of all the GymnasticBodies training components. This series starts off with quadrupedal exercises and gentle tumbling, including basic rolling skills, and moves into swinging, travelling, plyometric, and ballistic movements as you’re ready. Dynamic strength training is THE essential tool for transferring maximal strength into athletically usable power.

classInfo.title: Restore Series
classInfo.description: 10-minute sequences crafted to gently relieve tension in every area of your body. Use them to safely introduce stretching and prepare especially tight regions for focused mobilization and injury prevention.

workouts.title: Shoulders
workouts.content: Open the shoulders and create a healthy range of motion while improving posture. A 10-minute essential course for anyone who spends a lot of time sitting, especially doing work at a desk!

workouts.title: Thoracic
workouts.content: In just 10 minutes, you can begin building essential range of motion for healthy daily movement as well as mobility in the thoracic spine, a first step if bridge work is on your horizon.

workouts.title: Scapula
workouts.content: Use this 10-minute course to prevent pain between your shoulder blades, increase your range of arm movements and improve your posture.

workouts.title: Hips
workouts.content: A gentle 10-minute sequence to help create stability for walking and running, combat the effects of chronic sitting, and improve range of motion in your hips.

workouts.title: Quad
workouts.content: Tight quadriceps wreak havoc on our knees and low back by creating too much tension throughout the lower body. Use this 10-minute course to prevent chronic knee pain and reduce excessive muscle tension in the quadriceps.

workouts.title: Hamstring
workouts.content: Develop balance, prevent common issues such as hip and low back pain, and create better posture by spending 10 minutes focusing on hamstring health!

workouts.title: Ankle/Knee
workouts.content: Support your knees and ankles with this 10-minute course. Learn to squat, stand, crouch, jump, and walk with less effort, all while preventing common issues, like ankle rolling and chronic knee pain.

classInfo.title: Wrist Sequence
classInfo.description: In less than five minutes you can strengthen your wrists to prevent injury and properly prepare for wrist-intense workouts–like handstand or planche training. These often-overlooked but seriously vital joints should make an appearance in any warm-up, and this follow-along makes it simple.

classInfo.title: Stall Bar Intensive Stretch
classInfo.description: Looking for fresh ways to incorporate stall bars into your fitness routine? This 10-minute follow-along introduces six stall bar stretches that target and ignite the hamstrings, hips and thoracic spine.

classInfo.title: Advanced Core
classInfo.description: Test your core strength with this challenging 5-minute workout! This routine progressively increases the intensity of two classic positions, the arch and hollow, to deliver a big abdominal burn.

classInfo.title: Killer Legs
classInfo.description: Hit the hamstrings and quads while getting a "killer" leg pump with this quick but challenging routine. Get a powerful start with jumping lunges, before moving into targeted mobilities and finishing with a straddle-L hold in this 5-minute workout.

classInfo.title: Fundamentals Series
classInfo.description:
A 20-day introduction to Gymnastic Strength Training (GST). Learn basic body positions and explore ranges of motion uncommon in conventional workout programs. You’ll leave the course with the skills and confidence to succeed with moderate level GST workouts.

Purpose of Movements

These are not a pass/fail exam.

These movements have been selected to highlight mobility deficits which currently exist in your physical structure. By identifying these deficits we can then begin to take progressive action towards their resolution.

The expectations are most certainly not for you to be able to hit the ground running and perform these perfectly on your first day. That would be beyond unreasonable. For now simply explore and experiment with these movements. Do not attempt to force anything. Do not attempt to force perfection if you are not currently physically prepared to do so.
Rather note the areas in which you are tight and struggling, keep them in the forefront of your thoughts and we'll begin to gradually correct these deficiencies with patience and consistency.

workouts.title: Crab/Ape
workouts.content: Learn to execute the crab and ape movements. The crab position will test your shoulder extension mobility while the ape exercise will assess your ankle and hip range. Both of these movements will have you working into your best variation of the exercise, and moving across the floor in the positions.

workouts.title: Body Orientations
workouts.content: You’ll become proficient in four new body positions: front support, rear support, supine, and prone. Knowing what these terms mean, and practicing their shapes, will prepare you to use them as building blocks in more advanced movements

workouts.title: Wrist Mobility
workouts.content: In this lesson, you’ll move your wrists through a sequence of stretches created to help you regain your full movement ability in these key joints. When done consistently, these mobilities will prepare the wrists to be healthy and strong, even with additional pressure and load from movements like push-ups.

workouts.title: Body Positions
workouts.content: You’ll learn the positioning for a straight body, a tuck, a straddle, and a pike. These four movements serve as the base for many stretches and core exercises, so take your time getting comfortable with them!

workouts.title: Block 1 Review
workouts.content: Flow through the positions and movements you encountered over the last few days. Play with the different ways they can move into and support one another while increasing your familiarity with them.

workouts.title: Frog/Stiff Bear
workouts.content: Play with two new positions to rebuild mobility throughout the lower body. Frog will increase your hip, knee, and ankle range, while stiff bear will address any tightness in the hamstrings and low back.

workouts.title: Torso Rotation
workouts.content: Strengthen and stretch the obliques to create stable support for your torso and spine. Health in these muscles makes it easy to twist, turn, and bend your body any way you need to!

workouts.title: Calf Mobility
workouts.content: Create space through the lower leg with a couple of calf-specific stretches. Changing the knee position from straight to bent purposefully engages the two large muscles of the calves.

workouts.title: Hollow/Arch
workouts.content: Practice two key exercises for a strong, stable core, the arch body and hollow body. The positioning you’ll develop through these movements will transfer seamlessly to more advanced movements like arch-ups and body levers later in your training.

workouts.title: Block 2 Review
workouts.content: Put together the positions, stretches, and movements you learned over the last four lessons in this simple workout. Touch on each exercise to see how they are interconnected and continue to develop proficiency in them.

workouts.title: Lizard
workouts.content: Through this compound movement you’ll develop awareness of and build mobility in the hips and shoulders while also strengthening the core. As you move in lizard, consider the connection between this position and that of ape and frog, particularly in the hips.

workouts.title: Protract/Retract
workouts.content: Develop control of the shoulder girdle with these two shoulder blade movements. Awareness of these positions will come in handy for scapular shrugs and planks when you’re ready.

workouts.title: Thoracic Mobility
workouts.content: Learn about the three sections of your spine and move through a mobility meant to target your upper back. The thoracic spine is often a point of contention if you work at a desk or spend much time sitting, and the movement you learn here will help you to open up and find relief.

workouts.title: Elevation/Depression
workouts.content: Learn two new shoulder movements that are important for handstands, dips, and hanging exercises. Play with different arm positions to see how elevation and depression feel from a variety of angles.

workouts.title: Block 3 Review
workouts.content: Combine the movements from this block to solidify your understanding of the positions. Up the challenge by including some positions from previous blocks!

workouts.title: Inchworm
workouts.content: This multifaceted movement will create mobility in the hamstrings and shoulders while building stability in the core. Move through your best positioning while working to straighten the legs and open the shoulders over time.

workouts.title: Flexion/Extension
workouts.content: Move through two more shoulder positions that involve bringing the arms overhead, and behind you. These positions are essential for reaching movements, and increasing shoulder comfortability.

workouts.title: PPT/APT
workouts.content: These two pelvic positions involve tilting the hips back or tilting the hips under, and knowing the difference will help you create more stability in your movement. PPT is required for many exercises including your front support position. APT comes into play during arched movements, and in many lower body stretches.

workouts.title: Block 4 Review
workouts.content: Revisit the daily limber movements and remember– you can use this routine before any workout to get loose and warm. Finish by reviewing the other drills from this block before you finish Fundamentals!

workouts.title: Daily Limber
workouts.content: Use this routine to loosen your muscles and increase blood flow to your joints. The movements you’ll learn here can be used everyday to help unlock stiffness and increase mobility.

classInfo.title: Elements 1
classInfo.description:
Intro: Elements 1 is the first of a six part series to build basic strength and mobility. Within Elements, you will find 15-20 minute, easy-to-follow workouts that are doable for everyone! Create a fitness base and learn body control with movements like scapular shrugs to improve your shoulder range and tuck hollow body holds to ignite your core.

How to use: Elements 1 consists of five upper body and five lower body (which includes core) milestones. Work through these milestones at your own pace until you can comfortably complete the hardest (5th) workouts. You'll then be ready to move on to Elements 2.

classInfo.title: Handstand Challenge
classInfo.description: Begin learning to hold a handstand with this fun 30 day challenge. Each day will work a new variation to keep your training fresh and invigorating.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 1
workouts.content: Your challenge (video below) for this handstand is to get as close as you can to an L-Shaped handstand while keeping your toes on the wall.  Place your hands on the ground and walk your feet up high onto the wall.  Point your toes, and with your knees straight and feet together, slide your toes down the wall until you reach an L-shape in your handstand. Make sure to stack your shoulders on top of your wrists and keep your core tight and engaged. Hold for 30 seconds.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 2
workouts.content: Your challenge (video below) is to perform a handstand long hollow with your hands as far away from the wall as you can get them while maintaining good form.  Place your hands on the ground and walk your feet up onto the wall. Start as close to the wall as is comfortable. Don’t worry about getting right against the wall; we are more concerned with your shape. Slowly begin to walk your hands away from the wall, while maintaining the shape.  Handstands are developed by creating strong muscular tension in the right position. First, be sure your shoulder blades are rounded and pushed up toward your ears. Keep your hands shoulder-width apart, and elbows straight and strong. Try to maintain a tight core by engaging your abdominal muscles inward. Your hips should be tucked under. Lastly, keep your legs straight and hips squeezed.  Hold for 30 seconds.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 3
workouts.content: Your challenge (video below) is to get as close as you can to a straight leg v-up with toes pointed using a 12” strap.  A strong core is essential in any activity and is one of the key components to your perfect handstand. Not all core exercises are created equal. Quality of movement and precision are vital to increasing your strength and getting your handstand.  Start by laying on the ground with your strap overhead. Keep your legs together and toes pointed and then simultaneously compress your legs to your torso and loop the strap over your feet. Make sure to bring the strap all the way down to your hips on the descent. Reverse the movement by bringing the strap back over your feet and toes to the overhead position.  Do 10 repetitions.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 4
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Handstand Courses. Incorrect head position in your handstand is likely to throw you off balance. This is because everything is connected and your head is a part of your spine. This means if you are arching your neck, more than likely it will cause you to do a “banana handstand.” Something as small as head position in your handstand can keep you from making progress, so let’s get it right.  Start by kicking into a handstand against the wall. Find an arched neck position by tilting your head back and spotting the area between your thumbs with your eyes. Maintain this visual spot and slowly tuck your chin just enough so that you’re still able to see this spot through your eyebrows. Once you reach the position where you can just see your thumbs, you’ve reached your correct head position.  Do 10 repetitions and hold the last rep for 10 seconds to find correct handstand head form.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 5
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Handstand Courses. Your challenge is to kick into a handstand with your finger tips as close as possible to the wall.  Start by placing your hands as close as you can to the wall and make sure to keep your elbows straight as you kick into your handstand. Shrug in your shoulders and use the muscles in your back rather than kicking too hard to lift yourself up. Hold your handstand for 30 seconds.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 6
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Stretch Courses.Your challenge is to bring your chest as close as you can to the ground.  Start by stacking your hips right on top of your knees about 4 feet away from the wall. Place your hands 2 feet off the ground (knee level high). Slowly push your chest to the ground without moving your hands. Your hips may move slightly forward.  Hold for 30 seconds.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 7
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Handstand Courses.Your challenge is to get into your deepest butterfly stretch while in your handstand.  Walk your feet up the wall and find your handstand. Bring your knees out to the side into a butterfly position and push your hips onto the wall. Keep your hips, torso and shoulders all stacked in a straight line. Hold for 30 seconds.  Having adequate hip mobility will help with your press handstand progressions. This exercise is fun because you get to stretch your hips while upside down! Keep your hips open and your core engaged in order to avoid an arched back. This will allow you to keep a straight handstand line and prevent any strain on the lower back while practicing your handstand.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 8
workouts.content:
Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Handstand Courses. Your challenge is to get as close as you can to a perfectly aligned handstand with your torso facing the wall.

Start in a plank position with your feet against the wall. Walk your feet up onto the wall and find your handstand. Bring your wrists as close as you are able to the wall. While in your handstand, maintain the following alignment:

1.) Hands shoulder-width apart
2.) Elbows straight
3.) Shoulders shrugged
4.) Chin in the correct position (see challenge #4)
5.) Ribs hollowed or tucked in
6.) Glutes squeezed and hips tucked under
7.) Legs together and straight
8.) Toes together and pointed
Hold your perfectly aligned handstand for 30 seconds.

When your core is not properly developed, doing your handstand by kicking into the wall can cause your back to arch in your handstand. By doing your handstand facing the wall, be patient. Your core will get stronger by practicing and maintaining a strong line.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 9
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Foundation Courses. Your challenge is to lift your legs as high as possible while pressing your torso forward.  Begin by sitting on the floor with legs straight out in front of you. Bring your finger tips past your knees and lean forward. Keeping your chest as close to your knees as possible, lift your legs off the ground making sure to keep your knees straight, feet together and toes pointed.  Hold for 30 seconds.  Training your core in handstand will help you to find balance when upside down. This compression exercise from our Foundation Courses will teach you to strengthen and engage your abdominals.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 10
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Handstand and Stretch Courses. Your challenge is to stretch your shoulders while in handstand, with your hands as far away from the wall as you can get them.  Begin by walking your feet up onto the wall, belly side first into your handstand and stop about 1 foot away from the wall. Maintain your feet, hips and torso on the wall and stretch by pressing your chest forward until you make contact with the wall.  Hold the stretch for 30 seconds.  Handstand shoulder mobility is key. Most people are limited in their shoulder range of motion, especially when brining arms overhead. It’s important to make sure you take care of your mobility in the chest, back and ribs to allow you to develop your handstand further.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 11
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Handstand Courses. Your challenge is to point and flex your toes while keeping your heels and feet together in your handstand.  Kick into your handstand against the wall and then flex all your toes towards the floor. Next point them to the ceiling. Make sure to keep your heels and feet together during this point/flex exercise.  Do 20 reps and on your last rep, hold and point your toes hard for 10 seconds.  Keeping your toes pointed and feet together will help you maintain your handstand line and will encourage you to keep your legs and core engaged in your handstand.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 12
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Stretch Courses. In today’s handstand challenge, we want you to do a back roll and bring your knees as close as possible to the ground. This challenge will open up your shoulders and neck muscles prepping you for handstand.  Start by sitting on the floor. Carefully roll onto your back and then move your knees up and over your body until you reach your head. Bend your knees and see if you can bring them beside your ears. You should feel the stretch on your upper back and spine.  Hold this shoulder and neck stretch for 20 seconds.  Your neck may be tight from performing all of the previous exercises in this challenge. Having muscles that are sufficiently open will help you to achieve good shoulder shape in your handstand.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 13
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Handstand Courses. In today’s handstand challenge, kick into a handstand against the wall and then arch your spine by bringing your hips onto the wall behind you. It’s important to maintain your shoulders stacked over your wrists.  Start by kicking into a handstand, about a foot away from the wall. Slowly, push your shoulders to open by bringing them away from the wall. At the same time arch your back by bringing your hips onto the wall. Make sure to maintain straight legs during this movement.  Hold the stretch for 20 seconds.  This is a great handstand drill to increase shoulder mobility while opening your chest. When training our handstand we practice many of the strength elements by spreading the shoulder blades apart (also called protraction). To bring balance to this movement we also want to practice pinching the shoulder blades together (also called retraction).

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 14
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Handstand Courses. Your challenge is to get as close as possible to a knee tuck handstand WITHOUT losing your shoulders stacked on top of your wrists.  Start by walking your feet up the wall into a handstand. Slowly bend your knees out to the side ‘frog legs’ and then down together in front of your torso. Hold this tucked position for 10 seconds and then reverse the movement back to a handstand.  This drill is perfect for helping to refine your line by working with different shapes. To perform this drill correctly, make sure to maintain a flat back with your shoulders stacked over your wrists. This exercise will build your upper back and help you develop a solid handstand line.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 15
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Handstand One Course. Your challenge is to perform a wall wrist pushup with good form.  Start by standing about 3-4 feet away from the wall. Make a fist and then place your knuckles on the wall in front of you. Initiate the movement of the pushup by bending the elbows out to the side and opening your hands to bring the back of your wrist to the wall. Return to the top of the pushup by reversing the movement, rolling back into a tight fist.  Try to complete 10 reps.  During handstand training, the pressure of the entire body is placed on your wrists. You’ll want to make sure to incorporate wrist stretches and wrist strengthening exercises for your handstand into your routine to build mobility and strength in your wrists.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 16
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Handstand Courses. Your challenge is to do a handstand while keeping your hips and knees on the wall as you do knee curls.  Start by walking your feet up the wall into a handstand. Only go as far as you are comfortable and able to sustain. Press your hips and knees onto the wall and slowly bend your knees, bringing your shins past parallel. As you do the movement, be sure not to lose your hip position. Reverse the movement and bring your shins back onto the wall and find your handstand shape.  Do 10 knee curls, making sure to find your handstand after each rep.  This challenge will teach proper hip position in the handstand. Often times, when correcting or working on one portion of your handstand line, another part will come out of alignment to compensate. For instance, if you are practicing your handstand by arching your lower back, you will likely bend the hips in an attempt to balance your handstand. Gaining control of each segment of your handstand is vital to straighter line.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 17
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Handstand Courses. Your challenge is to perform your scapular rolls in a handstand, as smoothly as possible.  Start by walking your feet up the wall into a handstand and find your best handstand alignment. Begin by rolling your shoulders in one direction and then move them in the other direction. During the “roll” movement of the shoulders, make sure to emphasize and break down each part of the movement. Start with the shrug, then spread the shoulder blades, next focus on the depression of the shoulders and then finish the movement by pinching the shoulder blades together.  Roll your shoulders 10x in one direction and then 10x in the other direction.  Mobility in the scapula (shoulder blades) is one of the crucial elements required for a solid handstand line. A deep “shrug” during the handstand will push your upper body into the correct shape and take pressure off your shoulders and wrists.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 18
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Foundation Courses. Your challenge is to perform this stretch with hands as close as possible to the ground.  Stand with your legs 3-4 feet wide, your toes facing forward and feet parallel to each other. Clasp your hands behind you and with straight knees, slowly lean forward while bringing your straight elbows up and over your body.  Hold for 30 seconds.  Mobility, mobility, mobility. Shoulder mobility is rarely acknowledged in our everyday activities, even for those of us who are physically active. Your handstand has as much to do with mobility as it does with strength and control. This exercise will open open up your shoulders for a much needed stretch.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 19
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Handstand Courses. Your challenge is to bring your hands as close as you can to a “diamond shape” while in your handstand.  Start by walking your feet up the wall, belly-side first and find your best handstand alignment. Shift your weight as needed to bring your thumb and index finger to touch in a diamond shape.  Hold your handstand for 30 seconds.  It’s good to get into the habit of challenging your “handstand muscles” in different positions so you can build comprehensive and mobile strength. This narrow grip handstand targets muscles in the wrists and forearms which will help you have more control in your handstand.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 20
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Handstand Courses. Your challenge is to do your handstand and then hold it with your chin tucked.  Kick into a handstand and find your best possible alignment. Slowly tuck your chin towards your chest and gaze at your feet. As you maintain a chin tucked position in your handstand, make sure you are also in the correct hip and core position.  Hold your handstand with chin tucked for 30 seconds.  This exercise helps to bring awareness to your neck mobility while maintaining your handstand line. Your neck position controls the base of your spine during your handstand, so you want to ensure the neck is in the correct position.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 21
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Foundation Courses. Your challenge is to stay strong while holding for time at the bottom of your pushup.  Come into a strong pushup position on hands and feet. Make sure to keep your belly tight and hips tilted forward in PPT (posterior pelvic tilt). While maintaining this tight body position, slowly bring your nose, chest and hips about 2-3 inches from the floor by bending your elbows close to your side.  Hold the bottom of your pushup for 30 seconds and then push back up into a strong plank.  Today’s challenge will target your core and shoulders. Practicing holds will help you to develop your strength at a faster pace. It also gives you time to become comfortable in the position, find your best form, and breath through any challenges that may come.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 22
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Handstand Courses. Your challenge is to get into a solid non-arched, front split handstand.  Kick into a handstand and find good alignment. From this strong handstand position, slowly bring down one of your legs into a front split position. See how low you can bring your leg down without arching your back or bringing your back leg off the wall.  Practice your Front Split Handstand by doing 3 reps on both the left and the right leg.  Today’s challenge help you to understand what parts of your body need engagement when playing with different leg positions. Many times, when you move your legs in handstand, your entire body will compensate by arching, loosing your shoulder stack or falling out of your handstand line.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 23
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Handstand Courses. Your challenge is to practice the different shoulder positions of the handstand by exaggerating each one, all while maintaining a tight core.  Start by walking your feet up the wall, belly-side first into a handstand. Find your best handstand alignment with your shoulders stacked directly on top of your wrists. Slowly move into an overstacked position by bringing your shoulders forward past your wrists and fingers. Next, slowly move into an understacked position by bringing your shoulders behind your wrists and moving your chest towards the wall.  Do a few repetitions until your body begins to feel the difference between each.  We already know that most of our shoulders are fairly rigid and undertrained. Putting weight on the shoulders in multiple planes will build strength and mobility into much of your shoulder girdle.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 24
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Foundation Courses. Your challenge is to do your Single Leg Extensions with your hips OFF of the ground.  Start by coming to a seated position with your legs out in front of you and hands by your thighs. Keeping your knees straight and feet together, press down through your hands, and lift your hips off the ground. Next, while keeping your hips lifted, bend your knees into your chest and straighten and lock one leg at a time.  Do 5 reps on each leg.  In handstand, total body engagement is a must. For many of us, lifting our own bodyweight is a challenge. Use this exercise to begin learning how to engage the muscles of your arms, legs and core at the same time.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 25
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Handstand Courses. Your challenge is to do a supine arch hold.  Lay on your back with a towel (if on a hard surface) or frizbee (if on carpet) underneath your heels. Arch your spine strongly while keeping legs locked and together. Slide your heels towards your shoulders while bringing your chest and back off the ground. You will be balancing on only your shoulders and heels.  Hold for 30 seconds.  By now you realize how important core strength and shoulder mobility are. This drill will help you to work both simultaneously.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 26
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Handstand Courses. Your challenge is to perform a single arm handstand with your best alignment, facing the wall.   Start by walking your feet up the wall, belly-side first and find your best handstand alignment. Slowly shift your weight to one side, shrug into that shoulder and bring your opposite hand to your hip. Make sure that your hips stay in contact with the wall evenly and your knees and feet are together.  Hold your single arm handstand for 15 seconds and then switch sides.  This challenge will help you further increase your strength by putting more weight on your muscles. The key is to maintain the form we’ve been working on throughout the challenge.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 28
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Handstand Courses. Your challenge is to kick into a single leg tuck near a wall, WITHOUT using that wall for support.  Start near a wall in a lunge position with your right leg forward and arms overhead. As you kick into your handstand, keep your left leg straight the whole time and then take a hop off of your lunged right leg. Quickly bend the right knee into a single leg tuck handstand. Once in a balanced single leg knee tuck handstand, slowly bring your bent knee down even closer into your chest. Try not to use the wall for support.  Balance your handstand for as long as you are able and then switch sides.  This drill will help you to find the balance your handstand requires. In order to get more comfortable with balancing in the handstand, we need to take it further from the wall.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 29
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Foundation Courses. Your challenge is to perform your scapular rolls in a reverse plank while keeping your hips high.  Sit on the ground with your feet straight out in front of you and your wrists facing back and about 6” from your hips. Keeping feet and legs together, lift your hips off the ground into a reverse plank position. Make sure to keep your hips high and core engaged. Start with your shoulder blades pinched together (retracting) and then move your shoulders forward in a circular movement pausing at the top of each roll in a retracted position.  Do 10 rolls and then reverse the movement in the shoulders.  When practicing your handstand, the key is to maintain core engagement while finding proper shoulder positions.

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 30
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Handstand Courses. Your challenge is to kick into a freestanding handstand using your best form, WITHOUT using the wall for support.  The time has come to put it all together! Start in a lunge position with arms overhead. Kick into a handstand near a wall, trying your best NOT to use it for support. Make sure to keep your shoulders shrugged and rounded, your chin in handstand position and your knees and feet together with toes pointed.  Balance your handstand for as long as you are able and show us your results!!  A free standing handstand will require you to put all the movements you’ve been practicing together!

workouts.title: HS Challenge Day 27
workouts.content: Your handstand challenge for today (video below) is inspired by our Handstand Courses. Your challenge is to perform your first knuckle pushups on the floor.  Come into a strong pushup position with your core tight and glutes engaged. While maintaining this tight body position, keep your elbows straight and then lift onto your first knuckle and fingers, one wrist at a time.  Do 10 reps on each wrist for a total of 20.  This exercise can easily be translated into your handstand practice. While in handstand, you can alleviate some of the pressure on your wrists by distributing your weight onto your palms and knuckles during your handstand.

classInfo.title: 7 Minute Warm-Up
classInfo.description: Skipping your warm up should be out of the question, but if you want to hit the important points in seven minutes, this one will do the trick. Warm up and stretch all of your biggest muscle groups and be ready to jump into your strength work.

classInfo.title: HS Tuck
classInfo.description: Kicking into a handstand is just the beginning. Learn how to control your 'stand form from its base by testing your tuck. Tucks will show you if you're stabilized from your fingertips to your shoulders and whether your hips are really stacked. And tucks never lie.

classInfo.title: Lower Body Flexibility
classInfo.description: Limber up your legs and hips with this 30-minute follow-along flexibility sequence. Through static and active stretches, you’ll limber and lengthen the muscles of your lower body.

classInfo.title: Weighted Mobility
classInfo.description: Fast track your mobility progress by adding load to this 15-minute weighted full-body routine. Give special attention to the areas that need it most, including your wrists, neck, shoulders, and hips!

classInfo.title: Bands Series
classInfo.description: Strengthen and mobilize your joints to prevent common injuries. Bands classes will teach you how to use this valuable tool as part of a balanced workout routine.

classInfo.title: Buffer Zone 40
classInfo.description: After some much-needed limbering, fire up your core with body levers before transitioning to leg-strengthening squat variations. Top off this 40-minute burn with upper body endurance via wall-supported handstand conditioning and close it all out with focused flexibility practice.

classInfo.title: Total Body Conditioning
classInfo.description: If you’re looking to squeeze in a quick 15 minute workout and still condition everything, this circuit will hit the spot. It includes a quick warm-up and cool-down.

classInfo.title: Elements 3
classInfo.description:
Intro: Continue progressively overloading your workouts to steadily gain strength and muscle in this series of 15-30 minute follow-alongs. You’ll find many exercises, such as V-Ups, target multiple body parts, like your hips and core. Creating these connections helps you link these positions to the more advanced progressions to come!

How to use: Elements 3 consists of five upper body and five lower body (which includes core) milestones. Work through these milestones at your own pace until you can comfortably complete the hardest (5th) workouts. You'll then be ready to move on to Elements 4.

classInfo.title: HIIT #1
classInfo.description: Keep your heart rate high as you warm-up with this 6-minute full-body class. This HIIT warm up covers all areas of the body with lunges, squats, core and upper body exercises coupled with high knees. You’ll be ready to take on your GST workout after this follow-along.

classInfo.title: HIIT #2
classInfo.description: If a quick, full-body burn is what you’re after, you’ll find it here as you move quickly between exercises that target your upper body, core, and legs. Use this warmup to raise your heart rate and prepare your muscles and joints for your GST workout, or use it on it’s own to sneak in a HIIT movement session.

classInfo.title: Parallettes #2
classInfo.description: Get a full body stretch using parallettes as a tool to support your best positions and move a little deeper. Use this 12-minute class to cool down after a strength session, or to supplement your stretching routine.

classInfo.title: Parallettes #1
classInfo.description: Follow along as you incorporate parallettes into your conditioning through sliding, pressing, and dipping. Expect to work hard for the duration of this 7-minute class. Add it in to kickstart your conditioning days by increasing your heart rate and activating the muscles of your upper body.

classInfo.title: Weekly Shoulders
classInfo.description: Follow along with this prehab routine used weekly by Coach Sommer’s athletes to keep your shoulders healthy and strong. All it requires is a couple light dumbbells and a set of rings.

classInfo.title: Beginner Bodyline
classInfo.description: Learning bodyline is important to training handstand correctly. You can use this class to get very familiar with two positions: anterior and posterior pelvic tilt. These key positions are the backbone for effective core and upper body exercises. Use this class until these positions are second nature for you. This will make the rest of your training more effective because you will be able to easily find and keep proper form.

classInfo.title: Elements 4
classInfo.description:
Intro: Graduate from the floor in your core workout as you progress into hanging leg lift and arch-up variations, and trade in all the push-ups for some dipping strength gains! In these 10-30 minute sequences, you’ll start to really see and feel the results of the consistent work you’ve put in.

How to use: Elements 4 consists of five upper body and five lower body (which includes core) milestones. Work through these milestones at your own pace until you can comfortably complete the hardest (5th) workouts. You'll then be ready to move on to Elements 5.

classInfo.title: Hip Prehab
classInfo.description: Keep your hips healthy and strong while protecting against common injuries, aches, and pains. This short follow along moves your hips through their whole range of motion and creates strength through the whole range. All this is done through simple, standing leg raise variations that can be done anywhere. Use this class to prime your hips for squatting or other lower-body exercises, or as part of a longer mobility session.

classInfo.title: Elements 5
classInfo.description:
Intro: You’ll start to see the carryover of these movements to more advanced bodyweight skills. The line you create in your hollow body is the same one you’ll need for your front lever, same goes for the planche lean holds in relation to your planche. You may still have a ways to go before you reach these final positions, but feel accomplished as you bridge the gap into intermediate training!.

How to use: Elements 5 consists of five upper body and five lower body (which includes core) milestones. Work through these milestones at your own pace until you can comfortably complete the hardest (5th) workouts. You'll then be ready to move on to Elements 6.

classInfo.title: Intermediate Bodyline
classInfo.description: Continue to develop posterior and anterior pelvic tilt through 9 minutes of drills done in wall-supported handstand positions. Learning to find the correct alignment while inverted transfers seamlessly to your handstand training. You’ll need to be comfortable with these positions to correct your balance and find your stack in a handstand.

classInfo.title: 360 Core
classInfo.description: Enjoy a fresh take on core training during this 20-minute routine. You’ll complete a comprehensive core workout including arch-hollow rolls, arch-up variations, and leg lifts alongside several other movements. Your lower and upper abs, as well as your obliques and low back muscles will feel stronger than ever as you implement this core workout. Use it as a stand alone workout and consider following up with a full body mobility session.

classInfo.title: Stall Bar Stretch
classInfo.description: Use stall bars to find relief through deep stretches in your upper and lower body. You’ll weight your straddle and pike stretches by hanging on the stall bars. You’ll also stretch your shoulders using the stall bars to go deeper. This 6-minute class is perfect for those days when you’re feeling frozen and locked up. Use it to loosen up before your workout or to shake out tension after!

classInfo.title: Elements 6
classInfo.description: By now you’ve built awareness, control, and strength in your body that will transfer seamlessly into more advanced movement (like that found in Foundation 2!). You’ll reach the full expression of basic bodyweight dips, and gain unshakeable core endurance through full hollow body rocks. Congratulations on sticking through to the end of the beginning of your GST journey!

classInfo.title: Elbow Sequence
classInfo.description: Keeping your elbows healthy means better movement for both your straight and bent arm training. Taking care of these important joints is made simple with this 10-minute prehab sequence. Using just a light weight, or even a PVC pipe,  you’ll protect your elbows and prepare them to stay healthy and strong for strength training. Do this sequence as part of your upper body warm-up, or as an addition to your focused mobility training.

classInfo.title: Calf Sequence
classInfo.description: The Calf Sequence is perfect for students who are ready to increase the volume of prehab work for their ankle and calf muscles. Challenge yourself with 150 reps for three different variations of calf raises. Can you complete each without resting?   Note: This sequence is a progression from the 60r calf work found in the Front Split Series.

classInfo.title: Stretch Series
classInfo.description: 45-minute sequences crafted to develop full-body flexibility including Front and Middle Splits as well as Thoracic Bridge. Each routine gradually builds in intensity, making these challenging and productive for a wide range of students.

classInfo.title: Jefferson Curl
classInfo.description: Heal Your Posterior Chain Sitting all day is doing a real number on modern students and desk workers. Poor posture can curve the thoracic spine, and shortened hamstrings tug at the lower back, calves, and plantar fascia. The Jefferson Curl corrects and strengthens this entire system, and we've built a workout to warm-up and prepare each component for the weighted stretch
